messages.subject: shiny server occupies terminal
parts:
Hi, 

I have successfully deployed the shiny server on my machine and I can produce a webpage with my app. However, I am wondering if I am missing something. I started the server simply using:

sudo shiny server

When I do this the server starts up and the app is available, but the terminal is occupied by the process. I solved this by using the 'screen' command that opens the server in another virtual terminal that I can get out of, leaving the server running there and continue other business. 

Is this the way other's are running this server or is there a cleaner solution?

Thanks,
Thomas

messages.author: 9711d30301c32133
messages.subject: Re: shiny server occupies terminal
parts:
Hi Thomas,

Glad you were able to get the software setup. Running it interactively from a terminal is certainly one option but, as I'm sure you're finding, isn't ideal for a production environment.

Checkout the chapter on starting and stopping Shiny Server in our documentation. The gist is: it's usually preferred to run "always-on" server software like this as a background daemon that starts automatically when your machine boots. I'm not sure what distribution you're using, but you'll likely find that the init.d or Upstart scripts will make this much easier for you.

Depending on which system you're using, starting Shiny Server could be as easy as "sudo start shiny-server" which spawns a background process to run it. Hopefully the docs will explain everything you need to know.

Let us know if you have more trouble!

Jeff
